answer: A farm that wants 232 keys therefore burns 232 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the timber seed, the ledge timing is verifiable from the falcon record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 313 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
